newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan awards 2Q tender to buy diesel, fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan awards 2Q tender to buy diesel, fuel oil.

text.p: Pakistan's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources has awarded its tender to buy diesel and furnace (fuel) oil for second quarter deliveries to two Middle East oil firms and two European traders, industry sources said.
It bought a total of 450,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel from Saudi-based trader Bakri Trading, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keamari.
Pakistan purchased 400,000 tonnes of 3.5-percent sulphur, 180-centistoke grade fuel oil from Bakri Trading and Sharjah Oil Refining Co (SOR) of the United Arab Emirates, on a c-and-f basis to Fotco.
SOR took part in the Pakistani tender for the first time. Fal Oil Co which owns SOR has, however, been an active participant into Pakistan's tenders.
It also bought 300,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur, 180-grade fuel oil from Bakri Trading, Dutch trader Vitol and Swiss trader Glencore, on a c-and-f basis to Keamari.
Pakistan has decided not to award any 80-octane gasoline cargoes in this tender as the offer price was almost double what it paid in the last tender for the first quarter.
The best offer this time was $30 per tonne above MidEast spot naphtha quotes, c-and-f Keamari, compared with $16.745 per tonne premium in the previous tender.

In anticipation of better offers, Pakistan has issued another tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of either 80 or 87 octane leaded gasoline per month in May and June. The new tender for gasoline closes on March 31 and will be valid until April 5.

In its last tender for January-March deliveries, Pakistan bought 480,000 tonnes of diesel, 420,000 tonnes of 3.5-percent sulphur (125-grade) fuel oil, 50,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur (125-grade) fuel oil and 50,000 tonnes of 80-octane gasoline.
